messages.subject: get_global() within set_source()
parts:
Hi,

I'm having some trouble using get_global() within set_source(). The idea is that the arrival time should depend upon a global attribute (in this case "hazard ratio") being set by other trajectories within the model. In this particular instance, I actually only need the number the once - the simulation effectively terminates after this arrival (or rather, I throw out all data produced after it during post-processing), so I don't even need the attribute value at any time other than when setting the generator. My current code is this:

 set_source("standard_mortality", function() rexp(1, get_global(env, "hazard_ratio") / 2048)) %>%
 log_("debugging") %>%
 activate("standard_mortality")

(with some surrounding trajectory stuff setting other generators and attributes). 

The error message is "Error: 'standard_mortality' at 2.00: Evaluation error: there is no arrival running.". The log_() runs fine, so  my interpretation is that set_source() does exactly what it is supposed to, and sets the generator to generate arrivals at a rate function() rexp(1, get_global(env, "hazard_ratio") / 2048) - the problem (I think) is that when the generator fires up, it is calling get_global outside of a trajectory.

Is my understanding right? Is there a solution? I wondered if a standard-R variable work better than attributes in this case, but even if it would work, it didn't feel like a particularly elegant solution.

Many thanks,
Jacob

Your understanding is right, and a standard R variable is the solution.

Currently, set/get_global is just a shortcut for set/get_attribute
with a "global" parameter set to true, which means that an arrival is
queried to get the value. As you said, when the generator fires up,
there's no arrival running: the generator is running.

I'm planning to change that, because you are not the first one to
expect this (i.e., calling get_global from a generator) to work. As
you can see in [1], I'm planning to implement add_global, at the same
level as add_generator or add_resource, to easily set up global
variables at the beginning of a simulation (schedules will be allowed
too). This will give global variables their own "status", which will
allow me to unlink them from attributes.

Then, get_global won't be just a shortcut and should work in a
generator. This requires some work, so you should expect a couple of
releases until this is available.

[1] https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/158

Iñaki

Thanks! Good to know that's the right approach.

How should I go about modifying R variables from within a trajectory? My strategy was to define a function:

set_hazard <- function(.trj, mag) {
    hazard_ratio <<- mag
    return(.trj)
}

And then insert it into a trajectory:

esrd <- trajectory("esrd") %>%
    set_hazard(9.2)

But, perhaps predictably, this seems to set the hazard ratio during setup rather than when the arrival is generated. 

Thanks,
Jacob

Use any activity that accepts an R function (all of them, in fact). To
be conceptually consistent, I tend to use a timeout, because *doing
something requires some time*... but even if the change must be
instantaneous, you can return a delay equal to zero.

messages.subject: Re: get_global() within set_source()
parts:
Hi Jacob,

I had this same issue and just ironed out a solution today actually - I also use timeout() to modify the global R variable.

My example below - the variable I am modifying is idx:

idx <- 0
setBatch <- function(){
  idx <- idx + 1
  return(0)
}

And then within the trajectory I call the timeout before indexing the vector for my set_source call:

trj %>% timeout(function() setBatch()) %>% set_source('gallon_', batch_speeds[idx])

Hope this helps,
John
